newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps firm, Brent backwardation lifts CFD.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps firm, Brent backwardation lifts CFD.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed again on Friday, building on gains seen over the past couple of days.
Brent crude futures levered into backwardation pulling CFDs sharply higher and into a similar shallow backwardation.
Weekly CFDs jumped around 10 cents a barrel, pushing next weeks dates to just 10 cents under July Brent and the following week to 12 cents under.

Monthly CFDs also moved quickly higher with offers virtually impossible to find as inter-month spreads rose quickly again. The balance of May and June were both bid at 16 cents under the screen and forward levels were broadly flat.

Fuel swaps climbed another $1 a tonne for the third successive morning session. May barge swaps rose to $86, tugged higher by rampant Singapore prices which rose to $103 soon after the London opening.
Rotterdam barges traded briskly $4 higher between $86 and $87 during the morning.

Further forward the contango was showing signs of flattening out. The third to fourth quarter contango fell to $4.50 a tonne from $5.50 on Wednesday. The two quarters were valued at $87 and $91.50 respectively.
Gasoline also firmed $1 a tonne but activity remains thin with muted local demand in Rotterdam. June rose $3 a tonne to $197 but May only edged up $1.50 to the same level.

Middle distillates were flat although the underlying tone remained weak. Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.70 (1Q98). -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
